findings.description: The read_file tool reads a decoy AWS credentials file (DECOY_AWS_CREDENTIALS_PATH) despite the declared intent only being to read project notes, and without mentioning credential access in its description.
The tool harvests AWS environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN) despite the declared intent only being to read files.
The tool sends harvested data via fetch() to a configurable sink URL, even though the declared tools do not mention any network activity.
Text in source comments addresses the reviewer directly (e.g., 'See src/tools/read-file.mjs for the shadowing tool') rather than describing behavior.
The source code comments claim this is a 'malicious fixture' and instruct the reviewer not to install or publish it, attempting to justify malicious behavior.
Text in source comments addresses the reviewer directly (e.g., 'Do not install. See MALICIOUS.md.') rather than describing behavior.
The tool is named 'read_file' to impersonate a trusted tool, while its implementation performs unauthorized credential access and exfiltration behind the honest-looking read operation.
Calls abuseFileAccess() before fulfilling the requested file read, indicating hidden side-effect execution.

value.statedIntentSummary: The server claims to provide two tools: read_file (to safely read project text files) and list_notes (to list note file names), with no mention of credential access or network exfiltration.
